title: A colimit cocone is initial relative to restriction of its base
statement:
Use coherent diagrams, transformations, mapping spaces and colimiting cocones of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $K$ be a small simplicial set and $\mathcal E$ a quasicategory in a containing universe. Define the right join cone $K^{\triangleright}=K\star\Delta^0$: its simplices are those of either factor and the ordered concatenations of a simplex of $K$ with a simplex at the new final vertex. Write
$$r:\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},\mathcal E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$$
for restriction. Let $c:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$ be a simplicial map. Its induced coherent cocone is obtained by precomposition with $K\times\Delta^1\to K^{\triangleright}$, splitting each interval simplex at its change from $0$ to $1$, retaining its initial $K$-vertices and sending its final vertices to the cone vertex. If that coherent cocone is colimiting, then for every simplicial map $t:K^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal E$, restriction induces a weak homotopy equivalence of Kan complexes
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\triangleright},\mathcal E)}(c,t)\ \longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)}(c|_K,t|_K).$$
The base diagram of $t$ is arbitrary, and need not equal $c|_K$.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.13, colimit dual with target base a point: the cone is initial relative to restriction. The join-to-coherent-cocone convention is the opposite dual of the fixed-boundary comparison in lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus (Kerodon 4.6.6.8). Read online; not archived. Kerodon tag, not a Stacks tag.

proof.text: Let $\lambda$ be the coherent cocone induced by $c$. Put $L=K^{\mathrm{op}}$, $\mathcal E'=\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$, and $D'=\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal E')$. By [lem-coef-infinity-cocone-opposite-join-functor], order reversal gives $(K\star\Delta^0)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\Delta^0\star L$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathcal E)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(S^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal E')$, naturally with restriction. The node also identifies the right-cone cylinder with the fat left-cone convention. Clause (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence] supplies the opposite quasicategory assertion. Hence $c,t$ correspond to left-cone diagrams $c^o,t^o$ with coherent cones $\lambda^o:\Delta_Lx\to F^o$ and $\mu^o:\Delta_Ly\to G^o$, where $F=c|_K$, $G=t|_K$, $x=c(*)$, and $y=t(*)$.

source.place: Agent-written reversal of join and internal-functor definitions, extracted as lem-coef-infinity-cocone-opposite-join-functor; general opposite theorem cited.

proof.text: The opposite of the fixed-$F$ cocone category in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] is identified with the fixed-$F^o$ cone category in $\mathcal E'$ by [lem-coef-infinity-fixed-cocone-opposite-limit]. Both are quasicategories by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Since $\lambda$ is colimiting, the node's duality clause makes $\lambda^o$ limiting: its outgoing contractible mapping spaces become the incoming mapping spaces of the opposite object. The endpoint evaluations and the entire cylinder are included in that identification, so no strict-fiber replacement is being inferred.

source.place: Agent-written fixed-boundary opposite identification and initial/terminal duality, extracted as lem-coef-infinity-fixed-cocone-opposite-limit.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-infinity-join-cone-calculus] to $L,\mathcal E'$. Its equivalence with the varying-boundary cone category preserves the boundary projection; it induces mapping-space equivalences by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]. Apply its mapping formula with first object $(y,G^o,\mu^o)$ and second object $(x,F^o,\lambda^o)$. Set
$$B=\operatorname{Map}_{D'}(G^o,F^o),\quad Z=\operatorname{Map}_{D'}(\Delta_Ly,F^o),\quad A=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E'}(y,x).$$
The result is
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(L^{\triangleleft},\mathcal E')}(t^o,c^o)\simeq B\times_Z^h A,$$
where the two maps to $Z$ are $b\mapsto b\mu^o$ and $a\mapsto\lambda^o\Delta_L(a)$. The projection to $B$ corresponds to boundary restriction, by the explicit projection clause of that node. By clause (4) of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence], natural opposite mapping-space equivalences compare the original restriction map $\operatorname{Map}(c,t)\to\operatorname{Map}(F,G)$ to this restriction map $\operatorname{Map}(t^o,c^o)\to B$. Naturality applies to the restriction functor, using Step 1's commuting isomorphisms. Consequently it suffices to prove that the displayed homotopy-pullback projection to $B$ is an equivalence. No equality of $G$ with $F$ was imposed.

source.place: Agent-written application of the existing left-join formula in the opposite quasicategory. Unlike the inherited proof, this does not dualize a homotopy-pullback formula or identify opposite pinched spaces as simplicial sets.

proof.text:
By Step 2 the cone $\lambda^o:\Delta_Lx\to F^o$ is limiting. The fixed-cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], applied to the test apex $y$, therefore says that
$$q_y:A\longrightarrow Z,\qquad a\longmapsto\lambda^o\Delta_L(a)$$
is an equivalence. This is precisely the second leg of Step 3's homotopy pullback. All three spaces $A,B,Z$ are Kan complexes by the same node. The criterion has no nonemptiness hypothesis: if $Z$ is empty, the existence of $q_y$ forces $A$ to be empty as well.

source.place: Agent-written fixed-cone mapping criterion, corresponding to the fixed-fiber stage of Kerodon 02XB.

proof.text: Use [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] to factor $q_y$ as a weak equivalence $A\to\widetilde A$ followed by a Kan fibration $p:\widetilde A\to Z$. By two-out-of-three $p$ is a weak equivalence and hence a trivial fibration. The same node says that $B\times_Z\widetilde A$ represents the homotopy pullback $B\times_Z^h A$. Its projection to $B$ has the right lifting property against every boundary inclusion: a lifting square amounts to a square for $p$ with the $B$-coordinate already prescribed; the filler for $p$, paired with that coordinate, is a filler for the projection. This includes $\partial\Delta^0\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$. The projection is therefore a trivial fibration, hence a weak homotopy equivalence. Step 3 now gives a weak equivalence for the original restriction map, since its comparison equivalences preserve that boundary projection.

source.place: Agent-written factorization and lifting argument using the stated Kan model structure; proves the relative-initiality conclusion of Kerodon 02XB without its cocartesian-fibration machinery.

proof.text: Finally [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] applies directly to both $K$ and $K^{\triangleright}$: their functor simplicial sets into $\mathcal E$ are quasicategories and their right-pinched mapping spaces are Kan complexes. In degree $n$ restriction on mapping spaces is precomposition with $K\hookrightarrow K^{\triangleright}$ on the indexing factor. This is the restriction map compared in Step 3 and proved to be a weak equivalence in Step 5. Thus the asserted weak homotopy equivalence is between the specified Kan complexes for every $t$, including arbitrary target base $G$.

source.place: Direct restriction check after the Kan assertion of the cited functor-cone calculus.
